summary: This is a pre-commit configuration file that sets up automated code quality checks to run before commits. It specifies Python 3.13 as the default version, then lists various linters and formatters (like black, mypy, and pylint) that will automatically validate code syntax, style, and type safety whenever someone tries to commit changes.

explanations.1: This tells pre-commit which Python version to use by default when running hooks that need Python.
explanations.5: This points to a repository of pre-built, commonly-used code quality checks that we can use without writing them ourselves.
explanations.17: The 'files' pattern means this particular hook will only run on files matching that path pattern (anything ending in .txt inside a .config folder).
explanations.27: Instead of pulling hooks from an external repository, 'local' means we're defining custom hooks that run tools already installed on our machine.
explanations.32: Language 'system' means the hook will run the command directly using whatever's installed on the developer's computer, rather than in an isolated environment.
explanations.34: Setting 'require_serial' to true forces this hook to run one file at a time instead of in parallel, which some tools need to avoid conflicts.
explanations.35: The 'args' list passes command-line arguments to the isort tool, in this case telling it to treat lines as valid up to 120 characters long.
